question: What torque should the gland bolts be tightened to when replacing the mechanical seal on P-101A?
expected_answer: 45 Nm in a star pattern (Rev 3; the older Rev 2 value of 40 Nm is superseded)

question: What is the set pressure of PSV-204?
expected_answer: 10.0 barg, confirmed in pop test INS-503

question: How many seal failures has P-101A had and what is the suspected root cause?
expected_answer: Three seal failures (WO-2201, WO-2214, WO-2257). Root cause traced to cavitation from low suction pressure; WO-2257 also found a partially blocked suction strainer. SOP requires PI-102 to read at least 0.8 barg before start.

question: P-101B just had a seal leak. Has anything similar happened on identical equipment?
expected_answer: Yes — sibling pump P-101A has had three seal failures with root cause low suction pressure/cavitation, and P-101B itself had one in January 2026 (WO-2233). Check suction pressure at PI-102 and the suction strainer first.

question: What is the minimum suction pressure required before starting P-101A?
What equipment is directly downstream of pumps P-101A and P-101B?
expected_answer: Both pumps discharge into a common header (with flow transmitter FT-103) feeding heat exchanger E-204, which feeds separator V-203.

question: Explain how a trip of K-301 can cause PSV-204 to lift.
expected_answer: K-301 compresses vapour from V-203. On trip, vapour backs up and V-203 pressure rises; at 10.0 barg PSV-204 lifts to flare. This happened in IR-2026-014: pressure rose 6.2 to 9.8 barg in ~4 minutes and PSV-204 lifted.

question: What was the root cause of incident IR-2026-014?
expected_answer: Degraded cooling water flow to the K-301 intercooler due to a fouled strainer, causing rising discharge temperature and trip. No intermediate alarm existed between normal operation and trip point.

question: Which statutory inspections in Unit 100 are overdue as of July 2026?
expected_answer: V-203 hydrostatic test (due 2026-02-10 per OISD-STD-128), PSV-204 pop test (due 2026-01-20; sent for recertification in WO-2251), E-204 tube thickness survey (due 2026-02-12), and K-301 performance test (due 2026-06-08). P-101A condition monitoring review was due 2025-09-15.

question: What is the design pressure of V-203?
What is the most frequent failure mode in Unit 100 work orders?
expected_answer: Seal leaks (SEAL-LEAK): four work orders — three on P-101A and one on P-101B.

question: Were there any early warning signs before the K-301 trip in March 2026?
expected_answer: Yes. Discharge temperature was trending up for at least ten days before the trip, and inspection INS-505 (June 2025) had already flagged the intercooler approach temperature trending up.

question: Which instrument measures pump suction pressure in Unit 100?
expected_answer: PI-102, on the common suction header from T-101.

question: A technician is about to restart P-101A after the third seal replacement. What should they verify, and why does it matter for this specific pump?
expected_answer: Follow SOP-U100-07 pre-start checks: PI-102 at least 0.8 barg, casing vented, start against cracked discharge valve, watch seal for 15 minutes. It matters because P-101A's three failures were caused by cavitation from low suction pressure, and WO-2257 found a blocked suction strainer — so suction condition is the critical check.
